## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-sparse`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-sparse)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-sparse`:

$$
2^{O((n+m)/\sqrt{\log(n+m)})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O((n+m)(\log\log(n+m))^2/\sqrt{\log(n+m)})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

| Quantity | Bound |

| Clauses | $O_{q,r}(n+m)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $3$ |

## Derivation

1. Represent each domain variable by q one-hot bits, enforcing the exactly-one condition with bounded-fan-in gates. Compute the truth value of each constraint with a constant-size circuit, because q,r are fixed. All gates receive width-3 equivalence encodings.

2. Add a linear-size sum of the m satisfaction indicators and a threshold comparison. The circuit and its gate-equivalence encoding have O_{q,r}(n+m) variables and clauses.

3. Binary search over the possible numbers of satisfied constraints, then fix variable values to obtain a realizing assignment. Polynomially many sparse-SAT calls give the stated exact bound and polynomial space.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- The m satisfaction indicators matter: this does not give A(n) or B(n) for arbitrary dense instances.
- No approximation error is allowed here, unlike an additive-approximation result.
- Binary objective weights require separate bit-length accounting.

The derivation must preserve the objective and account for the encoding length of numerical values; a decision consequence alone does not establish the stated optimization bound.
